verdicts.evidence: KICKOFF.md:131 'Use the context-restore skill to reload the last checkpoint. Then use the brainstorming skill...' (verified verbatim, and the same sentence recurs at KICKOFF.md:253, 300, 362, 567, 974, each immediately preceded by a bare `/clear` line at 245, 289, 339, 559, 961 and, for the first occurrence, line 123). Skill quote verified at SKILL.md:3 (frontmatter description): 'Use when asked to resume, restore context, pick up where you left off, or figure out where you were — restores the working context saved earlier by context-save, defaulting to the most recent state across all branches so a session can resume even after a worktree or workspace handoff.'
verdicts.reasoning: The skill's trigger surface (its description) is a user-intent trigger — 'asked to resume' — it has no concept of pipeline stage or sequence position. What KICKOFF actually supplies at each of these six sites is not restore methodology (the skill owns that fully) but *placement*: schedule a context-restore immediately after each of six specific `/clear` boundaries, as the first act of that pipeline step. A skill file cannot know, and does not assert, when in a 13-step pipeline it should be invoked; that is squarely the 'ordering / parallelism across skills' carve-out the adjudication rules name as load-bearing, not duplication. Confirmed as originally classed; low severity is appropriate since it's a short, uncontested clause repeated identically six times rather than a rich per-site payload.

verdicts.evidence: KICKOFF.md:131 phrase 'to reload the last checkpoint' (no title/number argument given at any of the six sites — verified against SKILL.md's own Detect-command block). Skill quote verified at SKILL.md:12: '**Default: load the most recent saved context across ALL branches.** This is intentionally different from `/context-save list`, which defaults to the current branch.' Corroborating restatements of the same default confirmed at SKILL.md:16 ('`/context-restore` → load the most recent saved context (any branch)') and SKILL.md:43 ('Otherwise → load the **first file from `sort -r`** — the newest timestamp prefix is the canonical "most recent"').
verdicts.reasoning: None of the six invocations passes a title fragment or number, so every one hits the skill's own no-argument default path, which SKILL.md defines completely and redundantly at three separate points. 'the last checkpoint' does not select among modes the skill offers (there is only one no-arg behavior) and carries no parameter the skill couldn't already produce on its own — a bare 'Use the context-restore skill.' with no trailing clause would resolve identically. This is the 're-derives the skill's own hard rule when the skill already enforces it' case, not a legitimate mode-selection or emphasis-of-optional-behavior case, since the skill's default is not optional — it's the mandatory behavior for the only invocation shape actually used here. Confirmed, but rightly scoped to low severity: it is a four-word clause, uses the pipeline's own established 'checkpoint' vocabulary (shared with context-save), and is not misleading — it just adds nothing beyond what invoking the skill bare would already do.
